text:
marco: Heads-up — since ~03:07 UTC we've had a sustained throughput drop (~35-45%) from the us-east inference shard g4-pool. Large number of worker restarts and a few GPU OOMs logged.

sana: seeing it too in dashboards. tail of the restart log shows repeated allocator failures then kernel fallback churn. pinging oncall.

devops-bot: [ALERT] cluster/us-east/g4-pool: throughput_degraded (35%) starting 2198765432. auto-scale not triggered because OOMs blocked new workers. Incident created: INC-2026-2198765432

harper: I pulled a short flamegraph and KV-cache hit-rate over the last hour. KV hit-rate dropped from 94% -> 70% right before the restarts.

jing: interesting — that KV-drop could increase memory churn (more cache fills -> larger allocations). Are we seeing more small-slab allocations?

marco: yes, allocator log shows slab fragmentation rising. snippet:
```
2026-03-17T03:09:12Z allocator: slab_free_ratio=0.12 -> 0.04
2026-03-17T03:09:14Z gpu_mem: used=86% total=48GB free=6.7GB
2026-03-17T03:09:15Z worker[2741]: OOM in fastpath allocate(8.4MB) -> fallback -> restart
```

sana: also correlation with yesterday's kernel-selection rollout (kernel-heuristic v2) that started at 02:50 UTC for a 10% sample in us-east. Could be a regress in kernel choice for small batches.

harper: profiling shows increased memcpy time and more kernel swaps in the hot path. partial trace:
```
kernel_select -> fast_gemm_int8 (chosen) -> memcpy backlog -> fallback to generic_gemm -> extra allocs
count(switches)=1275 in 7min
avg_dispatch_latency +12ms
```

jing: if fast_gemm_int8 is picking a kernel that fragments GPU memory for our typical prefix lengths, that would explain OOMs when KV cache tries to rehydrate many embeddings.

marco: mitigation proposal: 1) pause kernel-heuristic v2 rollout 2) force kernel whitelist: generic_gemm for pool for 30m 3) increase KV cache eviction threshold to reduce fills

ops-oncall: implemented 1 & 2. rolling config applied to us-east g4-pool at 03:22 UTC. monitoring.

devops-bot: [CHANGE] kernel-heuristic v2 rollout paused (target=10% -> 0%). whitelist applied: generic_gemm for pool us-east-g4 at 2198766120.

sana: after whitelist we see mem fragmentation trend reverse slowly, KV hit-rate climbing back to 88%.

harper: latency tail improved and restarts rate dropped ~80% within 15m. throughput recovering to ~95% of baseline at 03:40 UTC.

marco: we should capture full profiling traces and run a repro job with micro-batches and heavy KV churn. schedule a deep-dive tomorrow. filing follow-up: PERF-2026-33

jing: adding notes — possible causes: kernel heuristics preferring int8 fast path with larger temporary buffers, batching heuristics leaving many sub-8-token micro-batches, KV cache eviction policy thrashing under transient load. I'll create a repro harness.

harper: saved flamegraphs and allocator logs to /mnt/diag/2198765432/ — linking to perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood/2198765432

ops-oncall: incident marked mitigated at 2198769050. Will keep monitoring for 3h and collect traces.

marco: thanks all. postmortem will include root cause hypothesis + kernel-selection rollback criteria + a canary plan for future kernel heuristic rollouts.
